howToSteps.name: Enter Your Weekly Pay
howToSteps.text: Enter your gross ordinary time earnings per week (before tax). Do not include overtime, bonuses, or allowances unless they are regularly included in your pay. The ATO uses 'ordinary time earnings' for calculating the genuine redundancy payment.

howToSteps.name: Enter Years of Service
howToSteps.text: Enter your completed years of continuous service with this employer. Only full years count for the tax-free genuine redundancy threshold — part-years are not included. Your letter of redundancy or HR department should confirm this figure.

howToSteps.name: Enter Your Age
howToSteps.text: Your age at the date of dismissal affects the tax treatment. Genuine redundancy payments to employees at or above normal retirement age (67) do not qualify for the tax-free threshold — the entire amount is treated as an Employment Termination Payment (ETP).

howToSteps.name: Review Your Payout
howToSteps.text: The calculator shows the ATO's genuine redundancy tax-free threshold for your years of service, the taxable component (Employment Termination Payment), estimated tax, and your approximate after-tax payout. Note this is an estimate — the ATO applies concessional rates to ETP components.

faq.q: How much redundancy pay am I entitled to in Australia?
faq.a: The Fair Work Act sets minimum redundancy pay entitlements based on years of continuous service. The scale ranges from 4 weeks' pay for 1–2 years of service, up to 16 weeks' pay for 9 or more years of service. Employers with fewer than 15 employees may be exempt from the redundancy pay scheme. Your employment contract may provide more generous entitlements. Separately, the ATO's genuine redundancy tax-free threshold (currently $12,524 base + $6,264 per completed year) determines how much of your payment is tax-free.

faq.q: What is the genuine redundancy tax-free threshold in Australia for 2025–26?
faq.a: For the 2025–26 financial year, the ATO genuine redundancy tax-free limit is $12,524 (base amount) plus $6,264 for each complete year of service with the employer. For example, an employee with 10 years of service has a tax-free threshold of $12,524 + (10 × $6,264) = $75,164. Any redundancy payment above this threshold is an Employment Termination Payment (ETP) taxed at concessional rates.

faq.q: What is an Employment Termination Payment (ETP)?
faq.a: An Employment Termination Payment (ETP) is the portion of a redundancy or termination payment that exceeds the genuine redundancy tax-free threshold, or any payment that is not classified as genuine redundancy. ETPs are taxed at concessional rates: for those under 65, the first $245,000 (ETP cap for 2025–26) is taxed at a maximum of 30% (17% if your income plus ETP does not exceed $45,000). Amounts above the ETP cap are taxed at the top marginal rate of 47%.

faq.q: Is redundancy pay paid as a lump sum in Australia?
faq.a: Yes. Genuine redundancy payments are typically paid as a lump sum on or shortly after the termination date. The tax-free component does not appear in your assessable income. The taxable (ETP) component is subject to withholding tax by your employer, who will provide you with an ETP payment summary showing the tax withheld. You declare the ETP in your tax return, and any over- or under-withholding is reconciled with a tax assessment.

faq.q: Does long service leave get paid out on redundancy?
faq.a: Yes. If you have accrued long service leave, it must be paid out upon redundancy in most states and territories. Long service leave paid out on termination is taxed differently from genuine redundancy pay — it is generally taxed as ordinary income at your marginal rate, but with concessional treatment depending on when the leave was accrued. The redundancy calculator above does not include long service leave — add it separately using the marginal rate applicable to leave payouts.

examples.heading: 8 years service — $1,800/week gross
examples.text: An employee aged 45 earning $1,800/week gross ($93,600/year, 30% marginal rate) with 8 completed years of service receives a total redundancy payment of 14 weeks' pay = $25,200. The genuine redundancy tax-free threshold is $12,524 + (8 × $6,264) = $62,636 — the entire $25,200 payment is below the threshold and is fully tax-free. After-tax payout: $25,200.

examples.heading: 15 years service — $2,500/week, higher payment
examples.text: A senior employee aged 52 earning $2,500/week ($130,000/year, 30% marginal rate) with 15 completed years of service receives 16 weeks' pay (the maximum under Fair Work Act) = $40,000. The tax-free threshold is $12,524 + (15 × $6,264) = $106,484 — the entire $40,000 is below the threshold and fully tax-free. If the employer pays 30 weeks' pay ($75,000), the excess above the threshold ($0 in this case, as $75,000 < $106,484) remains fully tax-free.
